Visit note | 2025-06-22 03:00 PM | Dr. Arif Hossain, Pulmonology | Patient: Nurul Molla, 65, male. Mr. Molla attends for review and reports producing more sputum than usual along with wheezing on walking. He mentions these symptoms worsened after catching a cold at a crowded market in Mymensingh. He works as a tailor and has no known comorbidities. On examination, SpO2 is 89%, BP is 125/85 mmHg, pulse is 84 bpm, and weight is 68 kg. Chest auscultation reveals widespread expiratory wheeze. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up in 1 week, sooner if breathing worsens.

Visit note | 2025-06-22 03:00 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Priya Halder, 63, female. Mrs. Halder presents for her first visit reporting no pain, but rather early fullness and vomiting after meals, differing from typical discomfort. She states this started after weeks of taking painkillers for back pain in Old Dhaka. She works as a homemaker and has no comorbidities. On examination, her pain score is 7/10, BP is 123/73 mmHg, pulse is 76 bpm, and weight is 52 kg. Abdominal examination is soft with mild epigastric tenderness. Assessment: Peptic ulcer disease. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid painkillers such as ibuprofen, stop smoking, and eat regular meals. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a stool H. pylori test.

Visit note | 2025-06-22 03:00 PM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Jubayer Haque, 59, male. Mr. Haque comes in for his first consultation complaining of being unable to raise his arm and experiencing severe night pain in the shoulder. On physical examination, his shoulder lifts only to 95 degrees with restricted active and passive range of motion. Other vitals show BP 119/79 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, and weight 67 kg. Assessment: Adhesive capsulitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to start physiotherapy, do pendulum exercises daily, and apply heat before exercise. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.
